Question_text: BFF makes a range of computer screens that it sells to other manufacturers. The Managing Director has been looking at BFF's income statement. She is worried about the effects of an increase in the cost of materials. She said: 'Changes in technology have improved our production methods. BFF needs to remain competitive as imports of computer screens are increasing.' The Managing Director has to decide whether BFF should increase its prices.
Sub_topic: Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional
Increasing efficiency: automation, technology, labour skills
Changes from technology: computers in design, manufacturing

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'income statement'?
Identify the effect of an increase in the cost of materials on each of the following: Cost of sales: Gross profit:
Identify and explain two ways in which BFF's managers could use information contained in the income statement.
Identify and explain two ways changes in technology used in production could help BFF to remain competitive.
Do you think BFF should increase its prices? Justify your answer.

Question_text: WKN sells household goods such as plates and brushes. Last year sales in WKN's 200 shops increased but profit fell by 80% to $5m. WKN's Human Resources Director said: 'All retailers are finding this stage of the business cycle challenging. WKN has to reorganise the business. This will mean redundancy for 1800 shop workers. WKN plans to create 100 new jobs in the marketing department at head office to help maintain customer loyalty. The company is working with trade unions to carry out these changes.' WKN has to decide whether to select the candidates for the new jobs from the workers being made redundant.
Topic: 2.3 Recruitment, selection and training of employees
Sub_topic: Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump
Trade unions: definition, effects of membership

Parts.part_text: Identify two stages of the business cycle.
What is meant by 'redundancy'?
Identify and explain two ways a trade union could help WKN's employees.
Identify and explain two advantages to WKN of maintaining customer loyalty.
Do you think WKN should select all the workers for the new jobs from those about to be made redundant? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Keila owns a successful small bakery shop. Keila would like to expand her business. She could open a café selling cakes and drinks in a popular tourist location. Keila plans to give out free samples as her main method of promotion. She has prepared some customer and cost information as shown in Table 1. Keila used primary market research to find out some of the information.
image: Table 1: Forecast customer and cost information for the new café. The table has four rows (Average amount spent per customer, Average number of customers per week, Variable costs per customer, Fixed costs per week) and two columns (item description, value). Values are $4, 325, $2, $500 respectively.
Topic: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis
Sub_topic: Classify costs: fixed, variable, average, total
Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Forms: advertising, sales promotion, influence on sales
Primary methods: postal questionnaire, online survey, interviews, focus groups
Importance: reward for risk, finance source

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'fixed costs'?
Calculate the forecast revenue per week for the new café.
Identify and explain two advantages to Keila's business of using free samples as a method of promotion.
Identify and explain one advantage and one disadvantage to Keila's business of using primary market research.
Do you think Keila should open the new café? Justify your answer using the information in Table 1.

Question_text: VXH produces a range of soft drinks made from fruit using batch production. VXH uses specialisation in its factory. The business has grown quickly over the last two years. VXH has increased the number of production workers from 40 to 80. This has increased the span of control for each manager. It has been difficult for VXH to keep workers motivated. The Human Resources Manager has to decide whether it is better to use job rotation or financial bonuses to improve employee motivation.
Sub_topic: Hierarchical structures: levels, span of control, chain of command, chain of tall/short
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion

Parts.part_text: What is meant by 'span of control'?
What is meant by 'uses specialisation'?
Identify and explain two possible reasons why VXH has grown quickly.
Identify and explain two possible reasons why VXH uses batch production.
Do you think VXH should use job rotation or financial bonuses to increase employee motivation? Justify your answer.
